record.paper_title: Initial boundary value problem for Korteweg-de Vries equation: a review and open problems
record.context_brief: Controllability under general KdV boundary conditions
record.original_question: For the finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries control problem based on u_t + u_x + u_xxx + u u_x = 0 for 0 < x < L and t > 0, with initial data u(x,0) = phi(x), and with general endpoint boundary conditions B_i u = h_i(t), i = 1,2,3, where B_i u = sum_{j=0}^2 (a_ij partial_x^j u(0,t) + b_ij partial_x^j u(L,t)) for real constants a_ij and b_ij, is the IBVP controllable under general boundary conditions, beyond the specific boundary-control configurations previously studied?

evidence.quote: with general non-homogeneous boundary conditions posed on the two ends of the interval (0,L)
Thus, with respect of the control issue, a natural and interesting open problem arises here:
Is the IBVP (4.18), with general boundary condition, controllable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Korteweg–de Vries equation on a finite interval (0,L) with L>0:
  u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0,  x ∈ (0,L), t > 0,
with initial condition u(x,0) = φ(x) for x ∈ (0,L), and three non-homogeneous linear boundary conditions of the most general form
  B_i u(t) := Σ_{j=0}^{2} ( a_{ij} ∂_x^j u(0,t) + b_{ij} ∂_x^j u(L,t) ) = h_i(t),  i = 1, 2, 3,
where a_{ij}, b_{ij} ∈ ℝ are fixed real constants (chosen so that the IBVP is well-posed) and h_1, h_2, h_3 are boundary data viewed as controls.

Question: For which choices of the coefficients {a_{ij}, b_{ij}} is this initial-boundary value problem (exactly or locally) controllable, in the sense that for any sufficiently small initial state φ and target state ψ in a suitable Sobolev space, one may choose h_1, h_2, h_3 to steer the solution from φ to ψ in finite time? In particular, establish controllability (or characterize its failure, including critical-length obstructions) for general configurations of the boundary operators (B_1, B_2, B_3), beyond the specific configurations (such as Dirichlet/Neumann boundary controls at x=L) for which controllability has already been established.
artifact.status_search_result: Controllability of the KdV equation on a finite interval has been established for several specific boundary-control configurations (notably Rosier's Dirichlet boundary control at x=L, with critical-length obstructions for the linearization, and recent resolutions for all critical lengths). However, no general theory covers arbitrary linear boundary operators B_i = Σ(a_{ij}∂_x^j u(0)+b_{ij}∂_x^j u(L)), and the problem is known to be highly sensitive to the choice of boundary conditions. Recent works (e.g., on coupled KdV systems and special boundary conditions) continue to address particular cases, suggesting the general controllability question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Small-time local controllability of a KdV system for all critical lengths
status_evidence.snippet: gives a complete answer to the longstanding open problem on the small-time local controllability of KdV on all critical lengths since the pioneer work by Rosier
status_evidence.claim: Controllability of KdV with specific boundary controls has been progressively resolved, but only for particular boundary configurations.

status_evidence.title: Boundary Effects on the Controllability of Coupled KdV Systems
status_evidence.snippet: The system is very sensitive to the choice of boundary conditions, and existing results do not give an immediate answer when considering different boundary condition combinations.
status_evidence.claim: General boundary conditions still pose open controllability questions for KdV-type systems.

status_evidence.title: Null controllability of a linear KdV equation on an interval with special boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: null controllability of linear KdV equations with special boundary conditions
status_evidence.claim: Only special boundary condition cases have been treated; the general case is not covered.
